hints.title: Most Significant Digit First Obstacle
hints.text: Digits are ordered from most significant to least without trailing pointers. How can auxiliary collections help you process values in reverse order without modifying the inputs?

hints.title: LIFO Digit Alignment Invariant
hints.text: Extract all digit values into last-in first-out order so the least significant digits can be added first with carry propagation.

hints.title: Head Prepending Carry Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Push all digits of list 1 and list 2 into two arrays. Pop from both while items remain or carry is non-zero, creating a new node with value sum % 10 and prepending it to the result list via node.next = head. Return head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def addTwoNumbers(self, l1: Optional[ListNode], l2: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        s1, s2 = [], []
        while l1:
            s1.append(l1.val)
            l1 = l1.next
        while l2:
            s2.append(l2.val)
            l2 = l2.next
        head = None
        carry = 0
        while s1 or s2 or carry:
            v1 = s1.pop() if s1 else 0
            v2 = s2.pop() if s2 else 0
            total = v1 + v2 + carry
            carry = total // 10
            node = ListNode(total % 10)
            node.next = head
            head = node
        return head
```

variables: N: number of nodes in l1 (1 <= N <= 100)
M: number of nodes in l2 (1 <= M <= 100)
complexity.notes: Extract digits into LIFO buffers and prepend sum nodes without modifying original input lists.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Reconstructing huge 100-digit integers overflows numeric limits in statically typed languages.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: LIFO buffers avoid mutating input lists and produce the result in linear time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ability to prepend nodes (node.next = head; head = node) to build the output forward without an extra reversal pass.
